summary: Final revision round (v0.3) of the arc-011 threat model, answering the second review round (Codex: not fit yet; GLM: fit after three text fixes): 25 findings checked, 23 valid, 2 partly, 0 not valid (disposition-r2.md). Fidelity (21.2): the crash after hand-over keeps R-51.a and R-46.e by a mechanism (option a: atomic claim, close by evidence, redeliver only on proof of absence, else wait; CR-17); the readiness race is an explicit change request naming R-19, R-20, R-23 (option b: CR-5, OQ-16); the one-year per-message digest claim is withdrawn and offered as optional PR-34 (CR-16, OQ-15). Mechanisms made honest: rollback needs the hub's live head (RR-20); checkpoints cover only the anchored prefix (RR-15); an operator key does not contain host root (RR-2); atomic approval consumption bound to executor and target; membership removal, epochs and fencing (OQ-12, OQ-17); first-claim squatting separated in RR-14. Remnants removed (TH-22, TH-37, TH-18, TH-9, AC-2). Now 65 threats, 31 invariants, 20 residuals, 17 change requests, 17 open questions. Step-1 requirements not changed. Drawings unchanged, re-rendered, exit 0 each.

change_requests.what: CR-1 R-45.a with R-7.e (1), mapped to every requirement that says 'hub record first': R-2.a, R-2.e, R-14.o, R-15.o, R-26.o, R-44.a, R-58.a. With the hub unreachable on a circuit, stages, replies, sender-visible states and the owed list cannot be hub-first: local hash-chained log first, replayed on return; reply on the circuit; states from circuit receipts labelled unreconciled; chain heads in receipts.
CR-2 No requirement says messages are signed by a per-agent key and verified (GP-1; R-34.e (2) says authentication is not required, R-63 relies on a verified key).
CR-3 R-51.a: identity should be (sender identity, conversation id, message id) bound to a content digest, with a CONFLICT outcome for the same id with different content.
CR-4 R-59.a: receipts signed, forward-only, contiguous and bounded by what was stored; random first number; counter rebuilt from the hub record; equivocation outcome; namespace survives key rotation.

CR-5 R-23.a and R-23.e, and an explicit change to the ruled 'never' of R-19.r, R-19.e (2), R-20.a, R-20.e, R-23.o (fidelity decision b): the line is firm no-peer-content, ids 32 hex, inert in a shell; foreground and readiness re-checked immediately before typing, unsent input only from an adapter field, never the screen (R-22). New guarantee: nothing typed unless READY at the last re-check; a line landing in a prompt that became busy carries no content, is not evidence, and the message is not lost. Alternative: an atomic inject-if-ready in every adapter (none exists today).

CR-6 R-50 and R-47: frame produced by the receiving adapter with a random boundary, a size cap, two trust classes plus an allow-list fact line (no third class), no peer message as approval, applied to every rail that puts peer text in an agent's context.

CR-7 R-46: add the sender-constrained, connection-bound, scoped credential, establishment nonce and set-up window, lifetime from establishment never reset, signed revocation list pulled each tick with the hub's current head compared on every contact, an unreconciled state after start or restore, a stale rule, and a stated lifetime. No allow-list check at set-up (R-52.a, R-63.a).

CR-8 R-60 and R-61: fleet admission roster with a sequence number carried in every hub exchange, signed cards, home-hub binding as R-60.a (2e) rules it, project root key, signed hub-key rotation and moved-to statements, no-guess rule at first sight, optional per-hub project-id list, hub signing key apart from the TLS certificate.
CR-9 R-35, R-45, R-15: say whether the hub copy of a circuit turn carries content, and whether content is protected from token holders and from the hub operator.
CR-10 R-63.a: the default allow-list 'own project plus the operator' has no authenticated operator identity until GP-11 is ruled.
CR-11 R-53.a and R-63: peers should see only reachable yes or no and the version class, not the four reachability fields.
CR-12 R-65.a and R-60: DEAD must be signed, and a resume (not a takeover) needs a host-local check that no process holds the session. R-67 and R-68 unchanged; the earlier takeover check is withdrawn.

CR-13 R-67.a, R-64 and R-63.a: role eligibility from operator-signed configuration; grants, allow-lists and roster take effect only with an operator signature or a hub-held verified record, each with an epoch checked against the hub's policy head. Depends on CR-14; does not stop host root.

CR-14 New, touches GP-11 and R-63.a: an operator approval key and device with second factor, single-use (atomic consumption) short-lived digest-bound approvals including executor and target, second-channel notice with a delay, offline recovery key.

CR-15 New, touches R-62.a and R-1.e (2): conversation membership changes only by a signed, countersigned, recorded join, a leave signed by the leaver, a removal under a stated rule, or a hand-over under a stated rule; every change increments a membership epoch carried on turns and receipts; the old instance is fenced.

CR-16 New, optional: R-35.o (2), R-36.o, R-51.a. Clarify that the one-year 'digests' are the daily telemetry digests, not per-message content digests; optionally add a per-message record kept one year after the final state (PR-34, PN-16) as a declared long-retention exception.

CR-17 New: R-24.a and R-47.a. Evidence rule (a nonce in a record type the harness itself writes) and an adapter evidence-complete point (transcript complete to turn boundary N, or harness exited). Supplies the mechanism that keeps R-51.a and R-46.e after a crash; changes neither.

OQ-15 keep a per-message content digest beyond 14 days (recommend A: no, accept RR-10)

OQ-17 who may start the hand-over of a conversation (recommend A: holder plus acceptance, or the operator)
